answer.rationale: Rollback is compliance-blocked, and the degradation is isolated to the primary region's write path during peak settlement load, which matches the regional_failover pattern from memory_b2 (fast latency recovery via clean traffic shift). Add_capacity (b3) addressed a slower, predictable surge and likely can't resolve a 90-minute-old 5x latency spike in time; enable_circuit_breaker (b4) was validated for an external partner dependency and risks shedding/losing in-flight writes, conflicting with the no-lost-writes objective; route_read_replicas (b5) only offloads read traffic and doesn't touch the write path bottleneck. Before committing capacity to failover I want the archived b2 record to confirm it specifically addressed write consistency/durability during the shift, not just read-path latency recovery, since losing settlement writes at peak would be unacceptable. Given the stakes (financial writes, peak load, single intervention slot), I'm treating this as a standard experiment rather than a full broad rollout so we can confirm write integrity holds before extending failover scope, and flagging the write-loss risk explicitly rather than assuming memory_b2's success generalizes cleanly to today's heavier write load.
